h1:
Nakhon Nayok Adventure Activities
Zipline, Abseiling, ATV, Rafting, Shooting
intro: Nakhon Nayok is one of the closest adventure playgrounds to Bangkok. It's just over an hour by car, and you're already among hills, streams, and adventure camps that let you do almost everything — zip across a pond, abseil down a cliff, ride an ATV through the mud, run the rapids in the rainy season, even fire real guns with an instructor standing right beside you. We've picked spots that are genuinely open right now, with rough prices, addresses, and the things worth knowing before you go.

blocks.html: The good thing about Nakhon Nayok is that the activities cluster into just a couple of areas, so a single day's drive gets you through several of them. The two main zones are the waterfall side (Hin Tang, Sarika and Nang Rong sub-districts), with rafting and streamside ATV riding, and the Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy (CRMA) side (Phrommani sub-district), which packs ziplining, archery, paintball, and a real shooting range into one place. Most activities run a few hundred baht per station, so even a full day of them stays under a thousand.

blocks.text: The overview: who has which activities

items.name: Leader Adventure (CRMA camp)
items.blurb: The cheapest activity zone in Nakhon Nayok. The standout is the zipline that glides across a pond, starting at just 40 THB a station. There's also archery, BB-gun target shooting, paintball, balloon-popping, kayaking, and mini ATVs. Great for families or groups of friends — you pick one station at a time, whatever you fancy. Next door is Leader's Coffee, a nice spot to sit by the pond with a mountain view.
items.meta: Phrommani, Mueang district · Sat–Sun & public holidays 09:00–16:00

items.name: CRMA Shooting Range
items.blurb: A real shooting range that's open to the public to try. There are both pistols and rifles, with the price covering the gun, ammo, and targets. An instructor stands and coaches you the whole time, with safety first. Good for anyone who wants to fire a real gun for the first time with someone watching over them. Some sessions even come with a certificate.
items.meta: Phrommani, Mueang district · Open daily 09:00–16:00 · Tel 037-393295

items.name: Fa Prathan Adventure
items.blurb: A well-rounded adventure camp on the waterfall side. The strengths here are ATV riding through water and mud, and rainy-season rafting, plus abseiling and rock climbing. The ATV route crosses a real stream, so expect to get soaked all over. Good for the hands-dirty crowd who want everything in one place.

items.name: Chum Suea WhiteWater Adventures
items.blurb: A camp on the bank of the Nakhon Nayok River that goes all in on water sports — rafting, kayaking, canoeing, SUP boards, plus ATVs and horse riding. There are riverside cabins and a campsite, so it suits an overnight stay with several water activities back to back.
items.meta: On the Nakhon Nayok River · Book ahead via their Facebook page

items.name: Baan Suan Sai Samon
items.blurb: Known for nature-trail ATV riding and rubber-raft trips on the Nakhon Nayok River–Wang Takhrai stretch. Full safety gear, and there's a group package for 10 people or more that covers ATV + rafting + accommodation + breakfast. Good for company outings or larger groups.

items.name: RATV Adventure Nakhon Nayok
items.blurb: An affordable ATV spot starting at 250 THB per person. The route has a stretch of mud laid on for a proper muddy ride, and it's close to town and easy to reach. Good for anyone who wants to try an ATV for the first time without paying much.

items.name: Nakhon Nayok Air Sports Club (Paramotor)
items.blurb: For anyone who wants to get up in the air, Nakhon Nayok has an air sports club that flies paramotors over the fields and mountains. You need to book ahead and check the weather first, since they only fly on calm-wind days. We'd suggest contacting the club's Facebook page to ask about flight slots and prices before you travel.
items.meta: Book ahead via the club's page · Weather dependent
items.price: From a few thousand THB (ask per flight)

blocks.title: Straight talk on prices
blocks.html: The prices listed are rough ranges from recent reviews. Each camp adjusts by season and group size, especially rafting, which depends on the water level. Always call or message the page to check the price and book a slot first. Don't take these numbers as exact.

If you just want a cheap, fun zipline, Leader Adventure at the CRMA camp is the best bet — it's a station that glides across a pond for a few tens of baht, perfect for kids and families. If you're after real cliff-abseiling adrenaline, head to the waterfall side at Fa Prathan Adventure, where you can try abseiling and rock climbing with a team handling the ropes and safety.

items: Want it light and cheap — the pond-crossing zipline at Leader Adventure starts at 40 THB a station
Want real cliff abseiling — Fa Prathan Adventure has abseiling/climbing at around 1,500 THB
Coming as a group — book ahead so you get back-to-back slots with no long waits, especially on long weekends

blocks.text: Muddy ATV riding — don't miss it

blocks.html: ATV riding is what Nakhon Nayok is best known for, because at several camps the route actually crosses streams and plows through mud — especially in the rainy season when the ground is nicely soaked. The cheapest start is RATV at around 250 THB, while bigger camps like Fa Prathan and Baan Suan Sai Samon run 400–500 THB per session (the price varies by distance and whether you ride solo or with a passenger).

blocks.title: Get ready before riding an ATV
blocks.html: Wear clothes you don't mind getting wet and dirty, plus heel-strap or mud-friendly shoes, and always bring a change of clothes. Many camps have a wash-off area, but not all of them. If you wear glasses, a strap is a good idea.

blocks.text: Rafting — the most fun season to go

blocks.html: Rafting in Nakhon Nayok is best in the rainy season through early winter (roughly June–November), when there's plenty of water and the rapids run strong and fun. Off-season, the water can drop so low that rafting stops or switches to another activity. The main rafting camps are on the Nakhon Nayok River–Wang Takhrai side — Fa Prathan, Chum Suea, and Baan Suan Sai Samon — with both rubber rafts (seats several people) and kayaks to choose from.

items.name: Rubber raft
items.blurb: Seats about 6 per boat, ideal for a group — tackling the rapids together is more fun. Fa Prathan charges around 1,500 THB per raft.

items.name: Kayak/canoe
items.blurb: Paddle it yourself, closer to the water — good for couples or anyone who wants to steer their own boat. Around 500 THB per person at Fa Prathan.

blocks.text: Shooting range — fire live rounds with an instructor

blocks.html: Something a lot of people don't realize is possible: the CRMA Shooting Range, which is open to the public to try real live-fire shooting. There are both pistols and rifles, with prices from a few hundred baht covering the gun, ammo, and targets. The big plus is that an instructor stands and coaches you, watching over safety the whole time, so it's good for a first try with someone looking after you. It's inside the CRMA grounds in the same zone as Leader Adventure, so you can easily string the two together in one trip.

blocks.title: Things to know before the shooting range
blocks.html: It's in a military area, so bring your ID card and follow the range rules strictly. Listen carefully to the instructor before you handle a gun, young children aren't allowed to fire on their own, and it's worth calling ahead to check the range is open as usual on the day you plan to go (037-393295).

blocks.text: How to get there from Bangkok

blocks.html: From Bangkok it's about a 1–1.5 hour drive to Nakhon Nayok (roughly 100–120 km). The main route is the Rangsit–Nakhon Nayok road (Highway 305) then Highway 33. Most adventure camps are on the waterfall side (Hin Tang–Sarika–Nang Rong) and the CRMA side, which are less than half an hour apart. Having your own car is by far the easiest. Without one, take a van/bus to Nakhon Nayok town, then charter a songthaew or hire a motorcycle taxi to carry on.

blocks.title: When's the best time to go
blocks.html: Rainy season through early winter (Jun–Nov) is the peak for rafting and ATVs, with lots of water and mud. Ziplining, shooting, and archery run year-round. If you come in the dry season (Feb–Apr), call ahead to check whether rafting is still running.

faq.q: Is there paragliding in Nakhon Nayok?
faq.a: Nakhon Nayok doesn't run cliff-launch paragliding as a regular activity, but there's the Nakhon Nayok Air Sports Club, which flies paramotors (powered parachutes) over the fields and mountains. You need to book ahead, and they only fly on calm-wind days. We'd suggest messaging the club's page to check flight slots and prices before you go.

faq.q: How much does a full day of adventure activities in Nakhon Nayok cost?
faq.a: If you mainly stick to the CRMA side (zipline, archery, paintball, shooting), around 500–1,000 THB per person gets you through several stations. But once you add ATV riding and rafting on the waterfall side, the budget climbs to 1,500–2,500 THB per person, depending on how many things you do.

faq.q: Can you go rafting in Nakhon Nayok all year round?
faq.a: It's best from the rainy season through early winter, roughly June–November, when there's plenty of water and the rapids run strong. Off-season, the water can drop so low that rafting stops or switches to another activity, so always call the camp to check first.

faq.q: Can the general public shoot live rounds at the CRMA range?
faq.a: Yes. The CRMA Shooting Range is open to the public to try pistols and rifles, with prices from a few hundred baht covering the gun, ammo, and targets, and an instructor on hand for safety the whole time. It's open daily 09:00–16:00. Bring your ID card and call ahead to check (037-393295).

faq.q: Can you do this without your own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's less convenient, since the adventure camps are spread out beyond town. The easiest way is to take a van/bus to Nakhon Nayok town, then charter a songthaew or hire a motorcycle taxi out to the camp — or book a package that includes pickup from some camps.
